failure_patterns.pattern: malformed_answer_json: Unparseable answers: stray `]` after each object (`]}],`), a filled optional list followed by a second `optional parameters` key, and a missing final `]` (news:94, ecommerce:108).

rejected_edits.content: 4. No list contains the same `name` twice. Two cases. (a) The schema says the param takes several values ('comma-separated', or a `publisher` / `category` filter): write ONE entry with the values joined by commas and no spaces, e.g. `publisher`=`cnn.com,bbc.com`, `category`=`science,technology`. (b) The param takes a single value (`location`, `email`, `domain`, `country`, `sku`): make one call per value, each its own object, with shared qualifiers repeated. 'COVID-19 stats for Egypt and the United States' -> two `Coronavirus Smartable: GetStats` objects, one with `location`=`EG` and one with `location`=`US` (BAD: one object holding both `location` entries).
rejected_edits.target: 4. No list contains the same `name` twice. BAD one call with three `email` entries, or `country` twice (US and GB). GOOD one call per value, each its own object.

rejected_edits.content: - TOPIC AND OPTION WORDS FILL FILTERS. A topic word in a clause fills the tool's category/topic filter even on a 'sources' or 'list' tool: 'US-based science and technology news sources in English' on `NewsData: sources` -> category=`science,technology`, country=`us`, language=`en`. With no topic named and 'top' wording, use the listed option `top` ('top English-language news sources from the United States' -> category=`top`, country=`us`, language=`en`). Copy enum values from the option list printed in the schema. 'Federal' or 'active' qualifiers on a politicians tool fill `level_of_government` and `active`.
rejected_edits.target: only when that call's own clause states or implies it.
